title: runtime.v1
description: The workload lifecycle contract between the control plane and the runtime kernel. Transport: HTTP. Every route except GET /health requires the caller credential (CallerCredential, as `Authorization: Bearer`). Every non-2xx answer carries an Error.

RuntimeState.description: The container/execution lifecycle state (NOT the workload's domain status).

CallerCredential.description: The value of `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every route except GET /health: the deployment's RUNTIME_API_TOKEN. The runtime, agent-api and meeting-api hold the same value; no workload receives it. Missing or wrong ⇒ 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` and an Error that names nothing else, compared in constant time. The runtime refuses to boot when the token is unset, shorter than 32 bytes, or a placeholder published in this repository.

CallbackSignature.description: The X-Runtime-Signature header on every RuntimeEvent the runtime POSTs to a callbackUrl: "v1=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, canonical(event))), where key = HMAC-SHA256(RUNTIME_API_TOKEN, "vexa-runtime-callback.v1") and canonical(event) is the RuntimeEvent as JSON with keys sorted, no whitespace and UTF-8 unescaped. The token itself never travels to a callback URL. A receiver that holds the token (meeting-api) refuses a callback without a valid signature with 401 and moves nothing.

SignedEventVector.description: A callback-signing vector: signing `event` with `token` must produce `signature` exactly.

token.description: a published test token; it authenticates nothing

RuntimeOwnedEnvPrefix.description: WorkloadSpec.env keys only the runtime may set: RUNTIME_K8S_* (Pod scheduling and Secret mounts) and VEXA_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_* (the workspace store's backing). A caller-supplied key with one of these prefixes is dropped, not refused. When the spec declares a mount set (VEXA_MOUNTS or VEXA_WORKSPACE_PATH), the runtime injects VEXA_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_TARGET and, when it has one, VEXA_WORKSPACE_MOUNT_SOURCE from its own configuration.

Error.description: The body of every non-2xx answer. 400: an unknown profile; VEXA_MOUNTS that is not a JSON array of objects each with a path; a mount outside the workspace store, or naming a host source this runtime does not serve; VEXA_WORKSPACE_PATH outside the store; a schedule job without request.url or without execute_at|cron. 401: the caller credential is missing or wrong. 404: an unknown workload or job. 422: a body that does not parse as the route's shape. 429: the owner's workload quota is full. 502: the backend could not start the workload; its status is already recorded stopped with stopReason start_failed. 503: the scheduler is not wired.

detail.description: a sentence for a human; never a credential

WorkloadSpec.description: The create() input. The kernel runs this as an opaque profile + env.

profile.description: opaque workload kind, e.g. meeting-bot | agent

env.description: config-by-env (12-factor); a workload's identity, topics and mount set live here, not as a kernel concept. Keys with a RuntimeOwnedEnvPrefix are dropped. VEXA_MOUNTS, when present, is a JSON array of {path, slug?, source?, …}: every path strictly under the runtime's workspace store, and a `source` only one the runtime is configured to serve; otherwise 400

WorkloadStatus.description: The kernel's view of a workload.

node.description: host / pod the workload runs on

RuntimeEvent.description: The lifecycle callback the kernel POSTs to callbackUrl on each transition, signed in the X-Runtime-Signature header (CallbackSignature).
